name: Strip Grip from Zombie
summary: Defending the Zombie pummel recovers the hand and elbow inside before the bottom player secures the knee hug and New York.
description: Defending the Zombie pummel recovers the hand and elbow inside before New York is secured. The relevant control is the high guard, not a lower-leg lockdown.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Zombie; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The relevant grips connect the hand, high leg and arm isolation. This is not a lockdown leg-release sequence.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): What is the early grip-defense objective?
flashcards.answer: Zombie seeks to clear the hand outside and close the knee hug; deny that arm relationship before the trap forms.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep both hand and elbow inside

plausible: Hand on chest; elbow drifts outside
Elbow low, wrist still outside
trap: Only wrist free after knee hug shuts

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): What should move as the wrist comes inward?
flashcards.answer: Recover the entire arm through available space rather than pulling the wrist while leaving the elbow fixed outside.
flashcards.answer_line: The elbow following toward the ribs

plausible: Shoulder rises, elbow stays on mat
Elbow moves toward their head
trap: Wrist curls round the pummeling hand

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): Which frame helps before the knee hug closes?
flashcards.answer: The early inside forearm occupies the space the pummeling hand needs and limits outside arm isolation.

plausible: Long arm reaches behind their back
Palm posted far outside their hip
trap: Hand on chest, forearm outside thigh

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): Where must the high leg loosen for later posture?
flashcards.answer: Opening the high-leg attachment creates slack for aligned head and shoulder recovery after the hand defense.

plausible: Only free foot; high thigh tight
Only between their fingers and palm
trap: Only knee base; high shin attached

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): When should you extract an already captured shoulder?
flashcards.answer: An arm caught under a closed knee hug needs slack before elbow withdrawal; stop if joint pressure has already developed.
flashcards.answer_line: Once leg loop lets the shoulder move

plausible: Once free hand finds a firm mat post
Stronger pull before leg opens
trap: Hand clear; elbow still in knee hug

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): What completes the useful arm-recovery checkpoint?
flashcards.answer: Restore inside arm position and safe posture after the high attachment opens; this prepares the next guard exchange.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow in; high upper-body hold freed

plausible: Hand free, shoulder pinned outside
Chin higher, leg loop unchanged

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): Which connection does the word grip refer to here?
flashcards.answer: The relevant grips organize the hand, high leg and knee hug. They do not define a lower-leg entanglement.

plausible: Head-side regrip after neck clears
Second leg clasps the head enclosure

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (top): After freeing your hand, what decides which guard remains?
flashcards.answer: Hand clearance changes one connection. The resulting guard depends on which high-leg and lower-body controls remain.
flashcards.answer_line: Remaining high and low leg controls

plausible: Whether your hand has any grip left
Whether elbow is inside their knees
trap: Only high-leg height, not low ankles

defender.name: Strip Grip from Zombie Defender
defender.description: Strip Grip from Zombie (defender): Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Zombie; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. The relevant grips connect the hand, high leg and arm isolation. This is not a lockdown leg-release sequence.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat. Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement. Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

When the hand pummel is stripped, rebuild guard retention with hip movement and an inside shoulder frame. Deny the crossface and chest pressure that could otherwise occupy the gap while you reach to recover the arm.

Prevent the return pummel: Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat.
Recognize New York: Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement.
Reset a blocked attempt: Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (bottom): What supports your pummel while they recover their hand?
flashcards.answer: Maintain the Mission Control posture connection while the free hand works; a loose high foot is insufficient.
flashcards.answer_line: High leg holds posture; knee braced

plausible: Foot hangs high while they sit up
Both hands chase wrist with leg down
trap: Ankle high while knee falls backward

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (bottom): Where can the hand-first pummel seek another opening?
flashcards.answer: Eddy's version works near the hand because the opponent can clamp more strongly directly at the elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Under hand, beyond the elbow clamp

plausible: Under elbow where clamp is strongest
Over wrist, press hand onto chest
trap: Hook their forearm from the outside

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (bottom): What should you guide instead of grabbing fingers?
flashcards.answer: Move the wrist-and-forearm line through available space to clear the inside frame without manipulating individual fingers.
flashcards.answer_line: Wrist and forearm to the outer mat

plausible: Elbow sideways, hand stays on chest
Hand up, forearm stays across chest

flashcards.question: Strip Grip from Zombie (bottom): Their hand reaches the mat; what prevents its return?
flashcards.answer: Follow the clearance by securing the arm wrap and supported knee so the opponent cannot easily bring the frame back inside.
flashcards.answer_line: Cover arm promptly with knee hug

plausible: Pause uncovered while changing grips
Let knee drift to reach farther
trap: Keep wrist contact; delay arm wrap
